title: Associated primes of a fractional principal intersection quotient in a normal domain
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $K$, and let $0\ne y\in K$. Put $J=A\cap yA=\{a\in A:a=yb\text{ for some }b\in A\}$. An associated prime of $A/J$ is a prime equal to the annihilator of a nonzero class in $A/J$. Then $A/J$ has no embedded associated primes: every associated prime $\mathfrak p$ is minimal among primes containing $J$, and each such $\mathfrak p$ has height one (there is a chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ and no longer chain ending at $\mathfrak p$) [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

proof.text: Write $y=a/b$ with nonzero $a,b\in A$. For $c\in A$, the equality $c=yd$ with $d\in A$ holds if and only if $bc=ad$. Thus $J=\{c\in A:bc\in aA\}$. This is an ideal, and it contains $aA$ because $bc\in aA$ whenever $c\in aA$. In particular $a\in J$ is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1, clauses (1) and (3); agent-written direct principal-quotient argument

proof.text: The $A$-linear map $A/J\longrightarrow A/aA$, $c+J\longmapsto bc+aA$, is well-defined by the displayed description of $J$. Its kernel is zero by the same description. If $\mathfrak p$ is the annihilator of a nonzero $c+J$, its image $bc+aA$ is nonzero, and for each $r\in A$ we have $rc\in J$ if and only if $brc\in aA$. Therefore the image has exactly the same annihilator $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1, clauses (1) and (3); agent-written direct principal-quotient argument

proof.text: Consequently every associated prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A/J$ is an associated prime of $A/aA$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-principal-quotient-associated-height] to the nonzero numerator $a$ in the original Noetherian normal domain $A$; it gives height one for $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 031T, lemma-normal-domain-intersection-localizations-height-1, clauses (1) and (3); agent-written direct principal-quotient argument

proof.text: The annihilator $\mathfrak p$ contains $J$, since each element of $J$ kills every class in $A/J$. If a prime $\mathfrak q$ satisfied $J\subseteq\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p$, then $a\in\mathfrak q$ would show $\mathfrak q\ne(0)$. Since $A$ is a domain, $(0)$ is prime; the chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ contradicts the height-one conclusion. Thus $\mathfrak p$ is minimal among primes containing $J$. If $J=A$, there are no nonzero classes and all assertions are vacuous.
